claims.text: Jamaica Plain Coffee offers a glimpse into the community’s vibrant tapestry.
In 2022, just around the corner at City Feed and Supply, a significant labor movement unfolded.
The workers formed City Feed Unite, demanding higher wages, healthcare, and COVID safety protections after their management cut pandemic hazard pay.
claims.evidence: In spring 2022, workers at City Feed and Supply formed City Feed Unite to demand higher wages, healthcare, and COVID safety protections after management cut pandemic hazard pay.

claims.text: David Warner and Kristine Cortese, the owners, refused to recognize the union voluntarily, which led to public protests and filings with the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB).

A year later, in 2023, another chapter unfolded nearby at 182 Hyde Park Avenue with the opening of Public Coffee Initially welcomed as a new addition to the local coffee scene, it was soon discovered to be affiliated with a plant for the Wesleyan Church.
These episodes paint a picture of Jamaica Plain as a community deeply engaged in social issues, where coffee shops are not just places to enjoy a brew but also arenas for activism and change.
Ula Cafe is a vibrant gathering place in Boston’s Jamaica Plain, weaving together the community’s past and present.

The nearby Haffenreffer Brewery, established in 1870 by German immigrant Rudolph Frederick Haffenreffer, was a cornerstone of Jamaica Plain and remained in the Haffenreffer family for generations until the mid-20th century.
This legacy of enterprise and community spirit continues at Ula Cafe, which reflects the neighborhood’s enduring values.
In November 2022, the café’s commitment to being a safe and inclusive space was tested when a transgender barista was targeted with a transphobic tirade.

In response, co-owners Marvin Mathelier and Beth Santos made a public commitment to protect their space, sending a community bulletin that announced immediate ejections for anyone threatening the safe environment they had cultivated.
This challenging event reinforced Ula Cafe’s role as a bastion of community values.
Another testament to this spirit is the 'Pay-It-Forward' wall, where customers can purchase meals or coffee in advance for those in need.
claims.evidence: Ula Cafe introduced a 'Pay-It-Forward' wall where customers can buy food or coffee in advance for strangers in need.

claims.text: Ula Cafe stands not just as a place to savor coffee, but as a living narrative of Jamaica Plain’s commitment to inclusivity and community.
Tres Gatos is not just a café; it is a living narrative of Jamaica Plain's vibrant community spirit.
In 2015, Tres Gatos became one of the first establishments in Massachusetts to introduce a mandatory 'Hospitality Administrative Fee' added directly to checks.
claims.evidence: In 2015, Tres Gatos became one of the very first restaurants in Massachusetts to introduce a mandatory 'Hospitality Administrative Fee' added directly to checks.

claims.text: By shifting part of the cost burden to patrons, Tres Gatos aimed to ensure equitable pay for its staff and sparked conversations across the local restaurant scene.
